questions.topic: Unmodified, Qualified, Adverse & Disclaimer Opinions
questions.prompt: Sufficient evidence establishes a material, pervasive departure from the reporting framework. Which opinion is ordinarily appropriate?

choices.text: Disclaimer solely because the error is known.

questions.explanation: An adverse opinion addresses a known material and pervasive misstatement.

questions.topic: Unmodified, Qualified, Adverse & Disclaimer Opinions
questions.prompt: The auditor cannot obtain evidence, and possible effects are material but not pervasive. Which opinion is ordinarily appropriate?

choices.text: No report because every scope limitation prohibits reporting.

questions.explanation: A material but nonpervasive evidence limitation ordinarily results in a qualified opinion.

questions.topic: Unmodified, Qualified, Adverse & Disclaimer Opinions
questions.prompt: Insufficient evidence could have material and pervasive effects. Which opinion is ordinarily considered?

choices.text: Adverse solely because evidence is absent.

questions.explanation: A disclaimer addresses inability to obtain evidence with potentially pervasive material effects.

questions.topic: Unmodified, Qualified, Adverse & Disclaimer Opinions
questions.prompt: Can an emphasis-of-matter paragraph replace a required adverse opinion?

choices.text: Yes, if the paragraph is long enough.
Only if the issue affects inventory.

questions.explanation: Emphasis draws attention to appropriately presented matters; it does not cure a material departure.

questions.topic: Unmodified, Qualified, Adverse & Disclaimer Opinions
questions.prompt: Which description best reflects pervasiveness?

choices.text: Any disagreement with a staff accountant.
Effects are fundamental or extend beyond a confined, limited aspect of the statements.

questions.explanation: Pervasiveness is a judgment about the reach and significance of effects, not a fixed dollar threshold.

questions.topic: Unmodified, Qualified, Adverse & Disclaimer Opinions
questions.prompt: A client refuses to correct a material but nonpervasive depreciation error supported by sufficient evidence. Which opinion is ordinarily appropriate?

choices.text: Unmodified because the error is confined.

questions.explanation: The issue is a known misstatement, not an evidence limitation; material but nonpervasive effects ordinarily support qualification.

questions.topic: Unmodified, Qualified, Adverse & Disclaimer Opinions
questions.prompt: Determine the ordinarily appropriate opinion for each independent scenario. Four findings: A: Evidence supports fair presentation with no material misstatement. B: A known departure is material but not pervasive. C: A known departure is material and pervasive. D: Evidence is unavailable and possible effects are material and pervasive. Assumptions: The auditor is independent. No law requires a different outcome. Consider ordinary financial-statement opinion consequences under the applicable auditing standard. Required: Opinion for A.
questions.explanation: Sufficient evidence supports fair presentation.

questions.topic: Unmodified, Qualified, Adverse & Disclaimer Opinions
questions.prompt: Determine the ordinarily appropriate opinion for each independent scenario. Four findings: A: Evidence supports fair presentation with no material misstatement. questions.explanation: The known departure is material but not pervasive.

questions.prompt: Determine the ordinarily appropriate opinion for each independent scenario. Four findings: A: Evidence supports fair presentation with no material misstatement. B: A known departure is material but not pervasive. C: A known departure is material and pervasive. D: Evidence is unavailable and possible effects are material and pervasive. Assumptions: The auditor is independent. No law requires a different outcome. Consider ordinary financial-statement opinion consequences under the applicable auditing standard. Required: Opinion for D.
questions.explanation: The evidence limitation has potentially material and pervasive effects.

questions.topic: Subsequent Events, Going Concern & Written Representations
questions.prompt: A post-year-end bankruptcy confirms severe customer financial distress existing at year-end. What accounting implication should the auditor evaluate?

choices.text: Adjustment of the year-end receivable valuation.
Automatic recognition only in the following year.
An automatic adverse opinion in every case.

questions.explanation: The later event may provide evidence about a condition already existing at the reporting date.

questions.topic: Subsequent Events, Going Concern & Written Representations
questions.prompt: A material fire after year-end destroys assets that were sound at year-end. What is ordinarily considered?

choices.text: Automatic adjustment of year-end depreciation for the entire loss.
Disclosure of a nonrecognized subsequent event.
A change to the prior-year tax return in every case.

questions.explanation: The fire is a new condition; material effects may require disclosure rather than year-end adjustment.

questions.topic: Subsequent Events, Going Concern & Written Representations
questions.prompt: Management proposes refinancing to mitigate going-concern uncertainty, but no lender commitment exists. What should the auditor do?

choices.text: Evaluate supporting evidence and feasibility of the plan.

questions.explanation: Mitigation depends on evidence and feasibility, not management intent alone.

questions.topic: Subsequent Events, Going Concern & Written Representations
questions.prompt: Written management representations are ordinarily dated as of which date?

choices.text: Only the first day of fieldwork.
A date chosen solely to precede all known problems.

questions.explanation: Representations should be appropriate through the report date and cover the relevant periods.

questions.topic: Subsequent Events, Going Concern & Written Representations
questions.prompt: What is the purpose of dual dating for a specifically identified subsequent event?

choices.text: To limit the extension of the auditor’s subsequent-event responsibility to that event.
To guarantee that all later events are immaterial.

questions.explanation: Dual dating limits the later responsibility to the specified event rather than extending the entire report date.

questions.topic: Subsequent Events, Going Concern & Written Representations
questions.prompt: Substantial doubt about going concern remains, but disclosure is adequate. Which statement is most appropriate?

choices.text: An adverse opinion is automatic in every case.
The applicable standard may permit an unmodified opinion with separate going-concern reporting.

questions.explanation: Adequate disclosure and the applicable standard govern the reporting; uncertainty alone does not automatically mean a departure.

questions.topic: Subsequent Events, Going Concern & Written Representations
questions.prompt: Evaluate four findings before issuing a nonissuer audit report. Events and representations: A: A January bankruptcy corroborates a debtor’s year-end distress. B: A February storm causes a new material loss. C: Management’s only refinancing plan has no lender support. D: Management offers a representation instead of available bank evidence. Scope: Assume the reporting framework requires recognition for evidence of existing conditions and disclosure of material new conditions. Evaluate the evidence and accounting implications before selecting an opinion. Required: Evaluate event A as evidence of.
questions.explanation: The bankruptcy corroborates prior distress.

questions.topic: Subsequent Events, Going Concern & Written Representations

choices.text: Automatic year-end adjustment in every case
Disclosure of a material new condition

questions.explanation: A new condition can be a material nonrecognized subsequent event.

Scope: Assume the reporting framework requires recognition for evidence of existing conditions and disclosure of material new conditions. choices.text: Assume written words eliminate audit risk

questions.explanation: Representations supplement rather than replace necessary evidence.

questions.topic: Report Elements, CAMs, KAMs & Comparative Information
questions.prompt: Which matter can qualify as a CAM in an applicable issuer audit?

choices.text: A material estimate discussed with the audit committee that involved especially challenging auditor judgment.
Only a matter that causes an adverse opinion.

questions.explanation: CAM criteria concern audit-committee communication, material accounts/disclosures, and especially challenging, subjective, or complex judgment.

questions.topic: Report Elements, CAMs, KAMs & Comparative Information
questions.prompt: Does communicating a CAM provide a separate opinion on that matter?

choices.text: Yes, it replaces the overall opinion.
Yes, it certifies the estimate’s exact future outcome.
Only when management asks for it.

questions.explanation: A CAM communication does not create a separate opinion or guarantee.

questions.topic: Report Elements, CAMs, KAMs & Comparative Information
questions.prompt: An auditor reports on tax-basis statements. What must the report appropriately identify?

choices.text: U.S. GAAP regardless of the basis used.

questions.explanation: Readers need to understand the basis of preparation and the applicable reporting context.

questions.topic: Report Elements, CAMs, KAMs & Comparative Information
questions.prompt: An appropriately disclosed matter is fundamental to understanding the financial statements. Which paragraph may be appropriate under applicable GAAS?

choices.text: A disclaimer solely because disclosure is important.
A paragraph stating disclosure cures every error.

questions.explanation: An emphasis paragraph highlights a matter properly presented or disclosed without replacing opinion analysis.

questions.topic: Report Elements, CAMs, KAMs & Comparative Information
questions.prompt: Which statement about KAMs in nonissuer audits is accurate?

choices.text: They are automatically required in every private-company audit.
Their use depends on the applicable reporting requirements or engagement terms.
They must always equal the number of accounts.

questions.explanation: Do not import a universal KAM requirement into every nonissuer engagement.

questions.topic: Report Elements, CAMs, KAMs & Comparative Information
questions.prompt: Prior-period statements were audited by a predecessor. What should the successor evaluate?

choices.text: Automatically claim responsibility for the predecessor’s work.
Ignore the prior period in all circumstances.
Use an issuer template regardless of standards.

questions.explanation: Responsibility for comparative periods and references follows the governing reporting standard.

questions.topic: Report Elements, CAMs, KAMs & Comparative Information
questions.prompt: Identify the correct reporting concept for each drafting note. questions.topic: Reviews, Compilations, Attestation & Compliance Reporting
questions.prompt: During a review, the accountant becomes aware of information suggesting a material misstatement. What is appropriate?

choices.text: Ignore it because reviews use only inquiry.
Perform additional procedures needed to determine whether a material modification is necessary.

questions.explanation: A review requires appropriate follow-up when information suggests material misstatement.

questions.topic: Reviews, Compilations, Attestation & Compliance Reporting
questions.prompt: Which service provides no assurance and is not an audit with reduced sample sizes?
questions.explanation: A compilation assists with presentation without providing assurance; its objective differs fundamentally from an audit.

questions.topic: Reviews, Compilations, Attestation & Compliance Reporting
questions.prompt: Which engagement requires suitable criteria for evaluating subject matter and may provide reasonable assurance?

choices.text: Every agreed-upon procedures report as an opinion.

questions.explanation: An examination evaluates subject matter or an assertion against suitable criteria and provides reasonable assurance.

questions.topic: Reviews, Compilations, Attestation & Compliance Reporting
questions.prompt: What is reported in an agreed-upon procedures engagement?

choices.text: The procedures performed and the findings.
An audit opinion on every financial statement.
A prediction of the company’s future profits.

questions.explanation: Users evaluate the reported findings; the practitioner does not express the broader assurance suggested by the distractors.

questions.topic: Reviews, Compilations, Attestation & Compliance Reporting
questions.prompt: A practitioner lacks independence in a compilation engagement. What should be evaluated?

choices.text: A rule that every compilation must become an audit.
A guarantee that the statements are correct.
The applicable disclosure and reporting requirements for the lack of independence.
A prohibition on all accounting services regardless of standard.

questions.explanation: Compilation standards can permit the engagement with the required disclosure of lack of independence.

questions.topic: Reviews, Compilations, Attestation & Compliance Reporting
questions.prompt: A financial-statement audit opinion is unmodified. Does that alone establish compliance with every federal award requirement?

choices.text: Yes, every unmodified opinion guarantees legal compliance.
Yes, unless audit fees exceed a threshold.
Only if the statements include a cash account.
No; compliance objectives and required procedures must be evaluated separately.

questions.explanation: Financial-statement and program-compliance objectives are not interchangeable.

questions.topic: Reviews, Compilations, Attestation & Compliance Reporting
questions.prompt: Review four proposed report descriptions before they are sent to clients. Engagement descriptions: A: A historical financial-statement review. B: A compilation with the required independence disclosure. C: An examination of subject matter against suitable criteria. D: Agreed-upon procedures on specified grant expenditures. Reporting objective: Select the assurance or reporting description supported by each service. Do not expand the scope beyond the engagement performed. Required: Description for A.
questions.explanation: A review provides limited assurance.
